name: Brimonidine drops (Lumify)

card.summary: Low-dose OTC brimonidine drops that shrink eye-surface vessels for whiter-looking sclera; FDA-cleared for redness, untested as a cosmetic.
card.note: Labeled for short-term redness relief only; forum users discuss frequent use and alternating with other drops, which no study has examined.

quick.overview:
Lumify is a low-dose brimonidine eye drop sold over the counter in the US for temporary relief of eye redness. In looksmaxxing circles it is used for a whiter sclera and a brighter eye look.
The redness-relief use is FDA-approved; use as a cosmetic enhancer, including claims about eye color, has not been studied.
quick.mechanism: Brimonidine is a selective alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that constricts blood vessels on the eye surface, reducing visible redness. Onset is reported at about a minute with effect lasting up to several hours.
quick.risks: Reported effects include itching, redness, dry mouth and rarer allergic reactions. Rebound redness has been described with the brimonidine rosacea gel; its extent with Lumify is not characterized. Labeling says it is for minor irritation, not glaucoma or serious eye conditions.

lead: Lumify is a low-dose brimonidine eye drop, brimonidine tartrate 0.025 percent, sold over the counter in the US for temporary relief of eye redness from minor irritations [2]. Brimonidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that narrows the small vessels on the eye surface, so the white of the eye looks whiter and clearer within about a minute and for several hours [2][11]. In appearance communities it is used for a brighter, whiter-sclera look, and some users also say light irises look different in colour [3][4].

The drug has long been used at higher strengths for glaucoma (patented 1972, medical use from 1996) and, as a skin gel, for rosacea redness [1]. Lumify was approved by the FDA on December 22, 2017 [2]. Randomised trials show redness falling more than with vehicle or saline, a pooled analysis reported no tachyphylaxis through day 29, and a pupil study found the drops constrict the pupil, more in light irises than dark [10][6][12].

No published trial has examined Lumify as an appearance enhancer or tested the eye-colour claim. Labelling describes it as a short-term redness reliever, not a treatment for glaucoma or serious eye conditions [2].

chain: Brimonidine narrows vessels on the eye surface
Visible redness falls within about a minute
Eyes look whiter and brighter for several hours
angle.text: The drops reduce visible redness, so the white of the eye looks cleaner and brighter in photos and in person. Some users add that pupil constriction and lower redness make lighter irises look more vivid.

paras: Lumify is the brand name of brimonidine tartrate 0.025 percent ophthalmic solution, made by Bausch + Lomb and sold over the counter in the US for temporary relief of eye redness from minor irritations [2][15]. Brimonidine is a selective alpha-2 adrenergic agonist; the same molecule is used at higher strengths in prescription glaucoma drops (Alphagan) and, in a skin gel (Mirvaso), for facial redness in rosacea [1]. Lumify was the first alpha-2-selective agonist approved for ocular redness [14].

The redness-relief label is the basis for its appearance use: when the small surface vessels of the white of the eye (the sclera and conjunctiva) are narrowed, the eye looks whiter and brighter. Sold products carry a label that the drops are not for glaucoma or other serious eye conditions [2].

Appearance communities use Lumify to make the sclera look whiter and the eyes look brighter. On looksmax.org one user explains the effect in German as a whiter sclera caused by shrinking blood vessels [4], and another reports that the drops make their light brown eyes look hazel [3]. A user taking isotretinoin, whose eyes had become dry and red, asked how often Lumify can be used and noted having read warnings against heavy use [5].

The manufacturer has also launched a cosmetic line under the Lumify Eye Illuminations name, a lash and brow serum, eye cream and makeup remover; a 2024 sponsored study of these products in irritation tests and 8 to 12 week use studies reported no safety signals [13].

Brimonidine drops lower intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension; the gel treats persistent facial redness from rosacea [1]. Combination eye drops pair it with timolol [1]. Lumify itself is labelled only for redness relief from minor irritations [2].

Brimonidine was patented in 1972 and entered medical use in 1996 [1]. The gel Mirvaso was approved by the FDA on August 23, 2013, and authorised in the EU in February 2014, according to Grokipedia [2]. Lumify, at 0.025 percent, was approved by the FDA on December 22, 2017 for over-the-counter sale, and a preservative-free version followed in April 2024 [2]. Before Lumify, over-the-counter redness relievers in the US relied on tetrahydrozoline (Visine-type drops) and naphazoline, which act at alpha-1 receptors, and the Medical Letter reviewed the new brimonidine product in 2018 [11][15].

In 2025, Bausch + Lomb ran a 578-participant Phase 3 non-inferiority trial comparing a brimonidine 0.025 percent plus sodium hyaluronate formulation with Lumify, and published a preservative-free versus Lumify trial in Ophthalmology and Therapy [7][14].

All three US over-the-counter redness agents constrict conjunctival vessels. Tetrahydrozoline is a selective alpha-1 agonist, naphazoline a mixed alpha-1/alpha-2 agonist and brimonidine a selective alpha-2 agonist [11]. Wikipedia reports that in glaucoma products brimonidine reduces aqueous humour production and increases drainage, and that its effect is peripheral rather than central [1]. Grokipedia reports onset within about one minute and effect lasting up to eight hours [2]; the Phase 3 preservative-free study likewise reported efficacy from one minute to eight hours [14].
Brimonidine is metabolised mainly in the liver, with an elimination half-life of about three hours after ocular use and about twelve hours after skin use [1].

An integrated analysis of four clinical trials of the 0.025 percent solution, two randomised, double-masked, vehicle-controlled efficacy studies (78 on brimonidine, 39 on vehicle) plus safety studies totalling 635 participants, found that investigator-rated redness fell by 1.4 units on a 0-4 scale on day 1 with brimonidine versus 0.2 with vehicle. Participants' own daily ratings also favoured brimonidine, and the authors reported no tachyphylaxis through day 29 and little rebound redness after stopping [10]. A 43-person University of Miami trial, which dropped Lumify in one eye and saline in the other, recorded none or mild redness in 41 of 43 Lumify-treated eyes at 30 minutes versus 26 of 43 saline-treated eyes [6].

The 2025 preservative-free comparison found the preservative-free formulation non-inferior to Lumify across eight timepoints on day 1, with comparable rebound redness rates in both groups and no severe or serious ocular events [14]. Several of these studies are sponsored by the manufacturer, and the Clinical Optometry review that describes the absence of tachyphylaxis was written by Bausch + Lomb authors [11].

sections.h: Effects on pupils, eyelids and eye colour
paras: Because users sometimes describe a colour change, the physical effects relevant to eye appearance have been looked at. In 28 healthy adults, 0.025 percent brimonidine reduced scotopic pupil size from about 7.3 mm to 6.4 mm, a 23.7 percent reduction in pupil area, and the constriction was larger in light irises than dark ones (37.6 versus 17.4 percent area reduction) [12]. In the eyelid trial, palpebral fissure height rose by roughly 0.2 to 0.3 mm in both Lumify and saline eyes, with no clear separation between them [6]. A planned Phase 4 trial will compare Upneeq and Lumify in acquired ptosis [8]. No published study has examined perceived iris colour after the drops; the pupil data are the closest measurement.

Wikipedia lists itchiness, redness and dry mouth with eye use, redness, burning and headache with skin use, and rarer allergic reactions and low blood pressure [1]. In the University of Miami trial there were six events in 43 people over 30 minutes after Lumify (dryness three, pain two, itch one) and two events after saline [6]. In the integrated analysis, reduced visual acuity occurred in 4.0 percent on brimonidine versus 4.3 percent on vehicle and conjunctival hyperaemia in 2.6 versus 2.9 percent [10].

Rebound redness is a recognised effect of alpha-1-acting decongestants; Wikipedia describes tetrahydrozoline as not suitable for prolonged use and says stopping it after tolerance has developed can bring redness back or worsen it [9]. Clinical Optometry authors state that tachyphylaxis was not observed and rebound redness was rarely reported with brimonidine [11]. Grokipedia reports that the Mirvaso skin gel can cause rebound erythema in up to about 9 percent of patients in long-term studies, usually resolving within 4 to 24 hours [2]; that figure is for the gel, not for Lumify eye drops. The product label states Lumify is for minor irritation and not for serious eye conditions [2]; clinicians generally evaluate persistent redness.

Lumify appears on looksmax.org as a low-effort eye-whitening step. One thread asks for sources in Austria and Germany and describes the effect as shrinking blood vessels to whiten the sclera [4]. A thread from a user on isotretinoin asks about frequency [5]. A third proposes alternating Lumify with a tetrahydrozoline drop to avoid tolerance and describes the aim as keeping the eyes looking striking while setting eye health aside; one reply objects that the other drop is stronger and causes rebound redness [3]. This is community discussion; no trial has tested alternating regimens.

No studies found of Lumify as a cosmetic whitening or eye-colour treatment. Studies of brimonidine 0.025 percent for ocular redness include the pooled analysis of four trials, trials against vehicle, a comparison with a preservative-free formulation and a Phase 3 comparison with a hyaluronate formulation [10][14][7]. Pupil-size and eyelid-position studies have also been done [12][6]. The Mirvaso rosacea gel has an observational study of 301 patients, of whom about 60 percent were somewhat or very satisfied at week 4 [16].

timeline.event: Tetrahydrozoline, the active in Visine-type drops, is patented [9].
FDA approves Mirvaso brimonidine gel for facial redness in rosacea [2].
FDA approves Lumify (brimonidine 0.025%) for temporary relief of eye redness, on December 22 [2].
The Medical Letter reviews OTC brimonidine (Lumify) [15].
Integrated analysis of four trials reports redness reduction without tachyphylaxis through day 29; a Miami eyelid-position trial begins [10][6].
Pupil-size study reports miosis after 0.025% brimonidine in healthy adults [12].
Preservative-free Lumify is approved; Lumify Eye Illuminations cosmetic products are studied [2][13].
Preservative-free formulation shown non-inferior to Lumify in a randomised trial; a Phase 3 comparison with a hyaluronate formulation completes [14][7].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org Lumify is treated as a redness drop for whiter-looking eyes, with questions about how often it can be used, where to get it outside the US and how it compares with tetrahydrozoline drops [3][4][5].

claims.claim: Lumify whitens the sclera by shrinking blood vessels.
claims.believers: Posters explain it as constricting visible vessels so the white of the eye looks cleaner [4].
claims.experts: Trials show lower investigator-rated redness than vehicle or saline over minutes to hours [10][6], consistent with its approved use for temporary redness relief [2].

claims.claim: Lumify makes light eyes look hazel or a different colour.
claims.believers: One user says the drops turn their light brown eyes hazel in appearance [3].
claims.experts: No published study has measured perceived iris colour; a pupil study found greater constriction in light irises than dark ones [12].

claims.believers: A poster states it rebounds less, while a reply says Visine is stronger and causes rebound redness [3].
claims.experts: Reviews attribute tachyphylaxis and rebound to alpha-1-active drops and report rare rebound with brimonidine, though the review authors are manufacturer-affiliated [11][10]; the preservative-free trial found comparable low rebound rates in both arms [14].

claims.claim: Alternating Lumify with another drop avoids tolerance.
claims.believers: A poster proposes alternating two different active ingredients to avoid building tolerance [3].
claims.experts: No study has tested alternating regimens; the integrated analysis covered use over about four weeks [10].

claims.believers: An isotretinoin user asks how often it is safe and cites posts warning against heavy use [5].
claims.experts: The label states it is for temporary relief of minor irritation and up to four times daily as needed [2]; clinical trials ran about four weeks with scheduled dosing [10][14].
